statements.subject: client
statements.description: A PAUSE request MUST be made either with the aggregated control URI for aggregated sessions, resulting in all media being halted, or with the media URI for non-aggregated sessions.
actions: use aggregated control URI when session.type = aggregated
use media URI when session.type = non-aggregated

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Any attempt to mute a single media with a PAUSE request in an aggregated session MUST be responded to with a 460 (Only Aggregate Operation Allowed) error.
actions: respond with 460 Only Aggregate Operation Allowed error

statements.subject: server
statements.description: After resuming playback, synchronization of the tracks MUST be maintained.
actions: maintain synchronization of all tracks upon resuming playback

statements.subject: server
statements.description: servers MAY close the session and free resources after being paused for the duration specified with the timeout parameter of the Session header in the SETUP message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The pause point after any PAUSE request MUST be returned to the client by adding a Range header with what remains unplayed of the PLAY request's range.
actions: add Range header to PAUSE response containing remaining unplayed range of current PLAY request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For media that is time-progressing and has retention duration=0, the follow-up PLAY request to start media delivery again MUST use "npt=now-" and not the answer given in the response to PAUSE.
actions: set PLAY request Range header to npt=now- instead of range from PAUSE response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The 200 OK response MUST include the Range header with the current pause point.
actions: include Range header containing current pause point in 200 OK response
